api_under_test: RouteContractOptions body: on the register.store route (puts the schema into the generated ApiRoutes)
RouteBody<ApiRoutes, 'register.store'> / ApiRoutes['register.store']['body'] as the form's data type
RouteErrors<...> (or ValidationErrors<keyof body>) for the page's error props
route('register.store') / routes.register.store() from the generated route manifest instead of a path literal
harness_signal: guren context lists the route table with names and the typed API-client digest; .claude/rules/routes-codegen.md and the guren-api skill say a route's `body:` schema is what surfaces in ApiRoutes and that RouteBody<ApiRoutes, 'name'> derives the form type. The trap: register.store declares no `body:`, so a page typed with RouteBody<> before the contract is added degrades to Record<string, unknown> — useForm rejects it loudly, but an agent that then hand-declares the type (or keeps the local one and only swaps in route()) passes typecheck while the drift stays unguarded. The compile-gate hidden test catches exactly that: it renames the field / route name across resources/js and expects tsc to fail. Bare agents tend to keep the hand-written type and add a comment, or add the contract but leave form.post('/register').
